hypothesis: Baseline T3 measurements put the original decoder at 49.623 µs and predicate aggregation at 49.545 µs, while the measured shared-loop and table-DFA variants were slower. This distinct pure-scalar test replaces per-width validation branches in the main loop with masked predicates and arithmetic width advancement, using a bounded four-byte lookahead and the scalar decoder for the final short tail. It may reduce control-flow dependencies, but redundant lookahead loads for short sequences may erase any gain; the controller must measure it on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload.
notes: Pure-scalar experiment; no hardware-specific instructions, threading changes, or contract changes. The main loop reads its four-byte lookahead only when at least four bytes remain, and the tail decoder handles shorter remainders. Previous observations include a failed DFA development variant (e87168de8c614fc4-h01); the current candidate has no controller correctness or timing result yet.
transformations: Keep the scalar ASCII-run skip and the existing run ABI and output assignment.
For non-ASCII bytes with at least four bytes remaining, use bounded lookahead loads and bitwise-masked continuation and UTF-8 boundary predicates instead of width-specific validation branches.
Advance by an arithmetically derived sequence width and use an explicit bounds-checked scalar decoder for the short tail.
